title: Commitment lease reconciler and staged shrink orchestrator for regional dedicated pools
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Customers with regional dedicated pools are purchasing throughput commitments (monthly leases) but we currently lack an automated, safe way to reclaim and reassign unused committed capacity when usage patterns change. This leads to both wasted reserved GPU capacity and brittle manual interventions during zone evacuations.

Goal: Build a centralized Commitment Lease Reconciler (CLR) and a Staged Shrink Orchestrator (SSO) that together reclaim or reallocate unused committed throughput while guaranteeing data residency and graceful failover. The CLR will compute reclaimable windows and generate lease adjustments; the SSO will execute multi-wave evacuations/shrinks that honor residency locks, commitment priorities, and autoscaler policies.

Scope:
- Centralized reconciler service that ingests reservation state, recent throughput telemetry, and customer SLA/commitment metadata.
- Lease reclamation algorithm: idle detection window, safe-reclaim buffer, staged-unlock tokens for residency constraints.
- Staged shrink orchestrator: evacuation waves, soft-drain vs hard-evict policies, priority lanes for committed workloads, and rollback triggers.
- Integration with autoscaler: policy hooks to convert reclaimed capacity into prewarm reservations or release quotas.
- Observability: per-lease metrics, audit trail for lease changes, and canary rollout dashboards.

Non-goals: full global rebalancer that migrates live KV caches between customer VPCs, or support for air-gapped on-prem upgrades in this iteration (we will provide hooks).

Constraints and considerations:
- Must never reassign or evacuate instances that are marked with an active residency lock token without explicit compliance approval.
- Minimize customer-visible request failures: prefer soft-drain (reject new routed requests) before hard-evict.
- Keep reconciliation decisions explainable and auditable for billing and support investigations.
acceptance_criteria: CLR runs hourly and produces a ranked list of candidate lease adjustments with justification metrics (idle_rate, recent_peak, safe_reclaim_margin)
SSO can execute a staged shrink across a 3-zone pool with configurable wave size and observe no >1% p99 latency regression for committed traffic during canary
All automated lease changes are logged in audit trail and surfaced in console with an explicit reason and rollback button
Integrations: autoscaler receives reclaim signals and either converts to prewarm reservations or releases capacity per policy
Safety: any residency-locked pool rejects automated lease changes and surfaces a human approval flow
comments: 2026-02-15 Maya Patel: Ticket created after ops postmortem — manual shrink during us-west outage took 4 hours. Proposal: CLR + SSO to reduce ops toil and preserve commitments.

2026-02-20 Lucas Chen: Initial design spike completed. Decided to centralize reconciliation to avoid split-brain; agents on each zone will execute wave steps from CLR directives. Trade-off: single control-plane increases blast radius but simplifies audits.
2026-02-27 Design review (Aisha Rao): Approved UX for console visibility and human approval flow. Requested to add explicit 'compliance reason' field when skipping residency-locked leases.
2026-03-02 Engineering sync: Chose safe-reclaim buffer = max(10% committed, 2 RPS equivalent) and default idle window = 72h. These are tunable feature flags.
2026-03-05 PR opened: platform#20345 implements CLR proto + reconciliation API. Requesting review from infra/security for audit format (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/20345).

2026-03-08 QA Canary plan: Run SSO in dry-run mode for next 48h on a non-critical regional pool (us-east-2). Measure p99 impact and validate audit entries. If green, enable soft-drain wave 1 for 5% of waves.
2026-03-10 Lucas Chen: Implemented residency-lock check and manual-override approval flow in console. Filed a follow-up ENG ticket to add HSM-signed approvals for enterprise compliance (ENG-779002).
